name: CortexDynamics VectorLink Pro Pilot Neural Interface
description:
The CortexDynamics VectorLink Pro is a full-spectrum vehicle neural link BCI rated for ground, air, and aquatic platforms, certified under Meridian 88's Unified Pilot Augmentation Standard (UPAS-7). The implant establishes a direct bidirectional data bridge between the user's motor and vestibular cortices and a vehicle's primary control bus, translating neural intent into control surface commands with a latency of under 4 milliseconds — approximately 18x faster than unaugmented stick-and-pedal response. The VectorLink Pro's proprioceptive extension layer maps the vehicle's sensor envelope onto the user's body schema, allowing a skilled pilot to perceive hull stress, engine torque, and aerodynamic load as tactile sensations distributed across their own body. A dedicated spatial co-processor handles three-dimensional positional modeling, providing continuous orientation awareness even during high-G maneuvers or underwater operations where visual reference is compromised. The unit supports simultaneous multi-vehicle management for licensed drone-fleet operators, with a branched attention protocol that partitions cognitive load across up to four concurrent vehicle threads.

The VectorLink Pro is the dominant professional pilot implant across Meridian 88's commercial aviation, courier logistics, and CorpSec aerial divisions, with CortexDynamics holding exclusive supply contracts with three of the city's five major air freight operators. It is the minimum hardware specification for pilots flying Tier 4 executive transport routes above the Spire approach corridors, where air traffic density and regulatory compliance requirements make unaugmented flight legally impractical. Among civilian pilots, the implant carries significant status — wearing a VectorLink Pro jack is an immediate social signal of professional certification, and the distinctive dual-port connector at the base of the skull has become a recognized mark of the pilot class. Street pilots and unlicensed courier jockeys who cannot afford the licensed version often seek out gray-market VectorLink units with the UPAS certification flags spoofed, a practice that carries serious legal risk but remains widespread in Tier 2-3 courier culture.
installation_requirements: Certified CortexDynamics installer or UPAS-accredited neurotechnician; pre-installation vestibular assessment; vehicle platform compatibility certification required for each rated class; 5-day neural calibration and flight simulation protocol
rejection_risk: Low — standard biocompatible housing with vestibular integration occasionally causing moderate motion-processing conflict during initial 2-4 week adaptation period
maintenance: Bi-annual UPAS compliance firmware update; connector port cleaning and impedance verification every 6 months; full system diagnostic required after any high-G incident exceeding 9G sustained

side_effects: Vehicular phantom limb syndrome — long-term users report feeling 'amputated' when not jacked into a vehicle, experiencing a persistent low-grade sense of spatial incompleteness

Vestibular recalibration disorder — during the first month post-installation, users frequently experience motion sickness in unpowered environments as the brain adjusts to the new proprioceptive baseline

Speed-seeking behavior — documented psychological tendency in experienced VectorLink users to compulsively seek high-velocity environments; classified as an occupational adaptation rather than a pathology by most Meridian 88 medical boards
Collision empathy response — some users report experiencing vehicle damage events as phantom pain, with severity correlating to the intensity of the proprioceptive extension mapping
cultural_context: Meridian 88's skyways are defined by VectorLink pilots — the implant has been in continuous production for eleven years and has accumulated a deep cultural footprint in the city's aviation and logistics communities. Pilot bars in the mid-tiers are identifiable by the rows of hardlink jacks visible at the back of patrons' skulls, and the informal greeting gesture among jacked pilots — tapping the connector port twice — has spread beyond the profession into broader Tier 3 youth culture as a gesture of mutual recognition. CortexDynamics sponsors the annual Meridian Open Air Rally, an illegal street-racing event held in the lower atmospheric corridors that serves as both advertising and a talent scouting pipeline for their professional development program.
known_users: Commercial airline and cargo pilots on Meridian 88 regulated air routes
Executive transport pilots serving Tier 4-5 clientele
Licensed drone fleet operators in logistics and delivery sectors
Gray-market courier jockeys running spoofed certification units
story_hooks: A CortexDynamics VectorLink Pro unit has been recovered from a crash site — but its onboard flight recorder contains neural telemetry data from the pilot's last moments that contradicts the official accident investigation report. Someone very powerful wants that data erased before it reaches an independent inquiry.

A veteran pilot's VectorLink has developed a rare feedback loop fault causing her to experience her aircraft's structural stress as genuine physical pain — she's been flying through it for months rather than ground herself, and she's now one bad flight from a fatal cognitive overload event. She needs a black-market hardware fix before her next mandatory medical check grounds her permanently.

The party needs to move cargo through a no-fly corridor controlled by a hostile faction's air defense network. The only pilot who knows the route well enough to fly it on neural link alone is a retired smuggler whose VectorLink certification has been revoked — they need the implant re-certified or spoofed, fast.
